title: INDIA Bloc Marches to Supreme Court, Demands Election Chief's Resignation Over Voter Rolls
excerpt: Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi led thousands toward the Supreme Court on Monday; stopped 600 metres short, opposition leaders filed a petition against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the voter-roll revision.
body:
• INDIA bloc leaders led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra marched toward the Supreme Court on Monday, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls.
  • Police stopped the march on Bhagwan Dass Road, about 600 metres from the court, after the Chief Justice declined a meeting and asked the opposition to file a petition instead.
  • Leaders including Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav filed that petition, alleging large-scale wrongful deletions — more than 130 million names have been struck from the rolls since the revision began.
  • The Election Commission denies favouring any party and says wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol; check your own enrolment status on the Commission's voter portal before the rolls are finalised.

India's opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court on Monday in the sharpest escalation yet of their campaign against the nationwide revision of voter lists, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a halt to the exercise they call "vote theft."

Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra led thousands of protesters through central Delhi under the banner "Chalo Delhi – March for Democracy." The march, which set out from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction, was stopped by police and paramilitary personnel on Bhagwan Dass Road, about 600 metres from the Supreme Court, where iron barricades blocked the route. Authorities had closed six metro stations for security reasons and imposed traffic restrictions across more than 20 stretches of the capital, according to Reuters.

A petition instead of a meeting

The opposition had sought a meeting with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to submit a memorandum. The Chief Justice declined, saying similar matters were already pending before the court and that no orders could be passed on the administrative side; he asked the leaders to file a petition through the judicial process. They did. The petitioners include Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress leader Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy joined the march.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wUeWokU616Q

"We will not back down."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, to reporters in New Delhi

What the fight is about

The Special Intensive Revision, under way since last year, has removed more than 130 million names from electoral rolls — a figure larger than Japan's population. The deletions include about 28 million people recorded as dead, 63 million who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced, according to reporting on the revision. The opposition, joined by the "Cockroach" youth movement that has protested in Delhi almost daily this month, argues the process disproportionately strikes eligible voters and benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. The march follows a weekend in which police detained thousands of protesters, an escalation covered in our earlier report on Gandhi's naming of Modi and Shah over the crackdown.

https://x.com/TheQuint/status/2109613254133891151

The other side

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and says voters who were wrongly deleted can re-enrol. The BJP has accused the opposition of trying to undermine India's democracy by questioning legitimate electoral processes. The government has not commented on Monday's petition specifically.

What it means and what comes next

For diaspora readers, the dispute is not abstract: many NRIs remain enrolled as overseas electors, and family members in India are among those whose names the revision has struck. Anyone whose name may have been deleted can verify and re-enrol through the Election Commission's voter services portal. The immediate test is now judicial. With the petition filed, the Supreme Court is expected to take up the voter-roll challenge through its regular process, while opposition parties say the street protests will continue until Kumar resigns and the revision is halted. Sources: Reuters' report on the Delhi restrictions, AP and Al Jazeera coverage of the march.
